scope: Proposition 4.8 (Deterministic hopping calibration) of the manuscript “Continuum Coulomb hardness with binary nuclear charges” (preprints/Continuum-Coulomb-hardness-with-binary-nuclear-charges-September-24-2026/Continuum-Coulomb-hardness-with-binary-nuclear-charges-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 275 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 290f40f845dc3e0d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 32. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let the contact layout be as in Lemma 2.4, choose one orientation per contact, and let the prescribed rational hoppings satisfy 0 < tmin ≤ tij ≤ 1, where tmin is an inverse polynomial in the source size. Let Z∗ be an integer with eD/2 ≤ Z∗ ≤ 2eD and round the nuclear charges as in Section 3. For inverse-polynomial τ, there is a deterministic polynomial-time procedure that computes rational centers Xi = Dpi + si obeying S := max i |si| ≤ Cm m + log D + log(1/tmin) + 1  + τ. (4.33) After applying Proposition 3.7 at these final centers, the resulting orbitals satisfy, on every chosen oriented contact, |Z∗Bij − tij| ≤ CtijEcal. (4.34) Here D is taken sufficiently large for the hypotheses above and for Ecal to be small. The reverse oriented attraction has an additional error at most 4e−0.86D in the same rescaled units. No additional geometric equation for the reverse orientation is needed.
